description: The platform for continuously improving AI agents.

summary.one_liner: Overmind is a platform that turns production agent traces or uploaded datasets into fine-tuned models and prompt/code optimisations, with observability, evals, and a unified inference API, and it can be self-hosted.
summary.what_it_does: Overmind instruments an AI agent's codebase with OpenTelemetry-based tracing via a Python SDK (pip install "overmind[tracing]") and scores traces as they arrive, matching them to agent capabilities. It builds versioned eval and training datasets from production traces or uploaded files, and lets you define per-capability eval metrics measured on live traces and in batch. It runs fine-tuning on Modal workers, benchmarks the resulting models against production, and serves them through one OpenAI-compatible API alongside frontier models. Optimisers run prompt, tool, and control-flow experiments in the repo, with the winning change delivered as a git diff. It exposes a REST API and an MCP server for Cursor, Claude Code, OpenCode and Codex, and the platform can be run locally with docker compose.
use_cases: Fine-tune a model on an agent's production traces
Add tracing and observability to an LLM agent
Evaluate agent outputs against custom metrics per capability
Run prompt or code optimisation experiments on an agent repo
Compare fine-tuned models against frontier models on real traffic
Self-host an agent training and monitoring platform
Manage agent datasets and evals from a coding assistant via MCP
how_to_run: export OVERMIND_API_KEY=ovr_… # project key from the Console
cp .env.example .env # set required keys (OpenRouter, Modal, inference, AWS, HF, sandbox)
docker compose exec api python manage.py seed_demo --owner <owner> # optional demo workspace
notable: Closes the loop from production traces to fine-tuned, served models benchmarked against your own metrics
MCP server with per-tool cost and destructive-action declarations, for Cursor, Claude Code, OpenCode and Codex
Split licensing: SDK and CLI under MIT, platform under AGPL-3.0, with self-hosting supported
Model weights are downloadable and retrainable by the user
Optimiser results are returned as git diffs in your own repo
caveats: Fine-tuning and serving require Modal workers, an AWS bucket, and several API keys before the API will boot
Hosted usage is metered; paid plans and credit caps depend on Stripe, which is optional for self-hosting
Self-hosted login is email/password only; Clerk and Stripe secrets are left blank
